rfm_tuples.f: Mode A — Verify auditor change and CFO/CAO turnover timing against EDGAR 8-K Item 4.01 / 5.02 filings + Form 4 reporting-owner changes

rfm_tuples.R: 'management identified a material weakness in our internal control over financial reporting that existed due to turnover of key accounting positions ... our internal control over financial reporting was not effective ... our report dated March 12, 2024, expressed an adverse opinion on the Company's internal control over financial reporting because of a material weakness.' Self-disclosed but the persistence (13+ months, two CFOs and two CAOs in scope) and the contemporaneous $101M+ prior-period error stream indicate an active accounting-quality problem, not a clerical issue. Forensic priority signal.

Q3'23 prior-reported loss of -$48.6M became -$62.0M As Corrected (28% larger loss). Errors primarily 'product returns and vendor credits' — classic working-capital quality red flag. rfm_tuples.interpretation: Multi-year, multi-line, cumulatively $80M+ restatement bundled as 'immaterial revision' and disclosed in the same filing that contains the adverse ICFR opinion. The pattern (errors found in Q3 AND additional errors found in Q4 of the same year) suggests the audit did not fully discover the population. The 'product returns and vendor credits' theme aligns with the supplier-finance exposure (see C5). Aggressive labeling.

rfm_tuples.R: 'On July 21, 2023, we entered into Amendment No. 2 to the 2021 Credit Agreement in order to amend certain financial covenants related to the Consolidated Coverage Ratio (as defined therein), and on November 20, 2023, we entered into Amendment No. 3 ... to further amend financial covenants related to the Consolidated Coverage Ratio.' + 'As of December 30, 2023, giving consideration to the amendments to our 2021 Credit Agreement, we were in compliance with the financial covenants required thereby.'
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A — Verify amendment count and step-down schedule against the agreement description in the filing; Mode B — derive: covenant amended twice in 4 months means the original covenant was already breached or about to be
rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-K Item 7 Liquidity (lines 516-547) + Note on Long-Term Debt
rfm_tuples.M_value: Two covenant amendments in 4 months (Jul + Nov 2023), both loosening the Consolidated Coverage Ratio. Stepped schedule: 1.75x through Oct 5 2024, then 2.00x through Oct 4 2025, then 2.25x — i.e. lender granted 18+ months of relief with a tightening back-end. 'Our compliance with these covenants will depend upon achieving our financial targets including improvements in operating income' — admits compliance is forward-dependent, not a current cushion. Operating income collapsed from $670M (2022) to $114M (2023, -83%), interest expense rose to $88M (vs $51M), so coverage ratio is structurally near the new looser floor.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Sequential covenant amendments are a textbook distressed-credit signal; the 1.75x->2.00x->2.25x step-up means lenders priced in re-tightening once operations recover — and recovery is not yet visible (op-income down 83% YoY). The 'in compliance' present-tense framing obscures that the company is in compliance ONLY because of the amendments. High severity for credit-quality angle.

rfm_tuples.R: 'As of December 30, 2023 and December 31, 2022, $3.4 billion and $3.1 billion of our Accounts payable were to suppliers participating in these financing arrangements ... Confirmed obligations outstanding at the beginning of the year $3,100,172 ... Invoices confirmed during the year 3,430,710 ... Confirmed obligations outstanding at the end of the year $3,361,249.' (Note 17 Supplier Finance Programs)
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A — Verify magnitude relative to total Accounts payable and Cash; Mode B — derive: at $3.36B supplier-finance balance vs $4.18B total AP, ~80% of AP is funded by third parties whose participation 'will reduce' if credit rating declines (per Item 1A risk factor)
rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-K Note 17 (supplier finance) + Balance Sheet (lines 703) + Risk Factor lines 496, 500
rfm_tuples.M_value: Supplier-finance program balance $3.36B = 80.5% of $4.18B total Accounts payable = 1.7x net long-term debt of $1.97B = 6.7x cash of $503M. Year-over-year growth: +$261M (+8.4%) while sales grew only +1.2%. Risk factor explicitly states 'further decline in our credit ratings would likely reduce the attractiveness of our supplier finance programs ... Lower participation ... would shorten our payable terms, resulting in an increase in our working capital requirements, and may have a material negative impact on our liquidity.' Credit ratings: S&P BB+ (junk), Moody's Baa3 (lowest IG) with NEGATIVE outlook.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Off-balance-sheet-flavored funding stack: $3.36B of third-party bank-financed payables on a $2.5B equity base. A one-notch downgrade by Moody's would push the company to high-yield at both raters, mechanically tighten supplier-finance access, and force a working-capital draw an order of magnitude larger than the $503M cash balance. This is the dominant Mode B finding for AAP — the framework's exclusion-of-liars discipline catches the asymmetric tail risk that management discloses but does not quantify alongside the rating-cliff dependence.

rfm_tuples.R: 'As of March 12, 2024, we had a credit rating from S&P of BB+ and from Moody's Investor Service of Baa3. The current outlooks by S&P and Moody's were stable and negative, respectively.' (Item 7 — Long-Term Debt)
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A — Verify split-rated status and that BB+ is sub-investment-grade by both Fitch/S&P scale conventions
rfm_tuples.M_value: BB+ (S&P) is the top high-yield notch — below investment grade. Baa3 (Moody's) is the bottom investment-grade notch — one downgrade = junk. NEGATIVE outlook by Moody's = >50% probability of downgrade within 12-24 months per agency conventions. AAP is therefore one Moody's action away from full high-yield status, which would trigger the supplier-finance contraction in C5 and likely raise revolver pricing under the rating-based pricing grid disclosed in Item 7.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Already split-rated, on negative watch with the investment-grade side. The fact pattern (covenant amendments, material weakness, prior-period errors, CFO/CAO turnover, op-income down 83%) is consistent with the negative Moody's outlook. Asymmetric: upside scenario is rating affirmation, downside scenario is full junk + working capital crunch.

Worldpac is the higher-margin Pro/import business — selling it would shrink margin mix even if cash-positive. Strategic-review framing softens what is functionally an asset-sale capital raise.

rfm_tuples.R: 'Net sales during 2023 were $11.3 billion, an increase of 1.2% compared with 2022, driven by new store openings and favorable product mix, partially offset by a 0.3% decline in comparable store sales.' + Operating income: $114.4M (2023) vs $670.3M (2022) vs $822.4M (2021). Net income: $29.7M (2023) vs $464.4M (2022) vs $596.6M (2021).
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A — Verify the framing 'driven by new store openings and favorable product mix' is the dominant explanation when operating income fell 83% on a 1.2% revenue increase
rfm_tuples.M_value: Operating margin collapsed from 6.0% (2022) to 1.0% (2023) — an 83% decline. Gross profit fell from $4,932M to $4,524M (-8.3%) on flat revenue, indicating gross margin contracted from 44.2% to 40.1% (-410 bps). SG&A rose from $4,262M to $4,409M (+3.5%) absorbing the inflation. Operating cash flow fell from $737M (2022) to $287M (2023, -61%). MD&A frames revenue narrative ('grew 1.2%') without proportional emphasis on the 410 bps margin collapse. AutoZone (peer) reported 1Q-3Q'23 operating margins ~20%+; AAP at 1% is industry-worst by a wide margin.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Revenue framing obscures a margin collapse that, combined with rising interest expense ($88M vs $51M) and tax floor (effective rate 6.6% — only because pre-tax income was tiny), leaves AAP earning $0.50 diluted EPS on a base where peers earn 20x+ that ratio. The 'favorable product mix' language is hard to reconcile with -410 bps gross margin.

rfm_tuples.R: Dividends paid: 2023=$209M, 2022=$336M, 2021=$161M. Share repurchases: 2023=$15M, 2022=$618M, 2021=$906M. (Cash Flow Statement)
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B — derive: drastic 2023 capital-return cut ($15M buybacks vs $618M prior year; dividend run-rate already lowered before 10-K filing) is a distress-implied cash-preservation signal, but the 10-K doesn't explicitly call it out as a defensive action

rfm_tuples.M_value: Buybacks dropped 97.6% YoY ($618M -> $15M). Cumulative 2021-22-23 dividends + buybacks = $161+336+161+906+618+15 = $2.2B over 3 years on a current equity base of $2.5B — i.e., capital returns roughly equal to current total equity. With operating cash flow of $287M now barely covering capex ($242M) + interest ($88M) + remaining dividend (~$209M), the dividend itself is uncovered by free cash flow ex-working-capital, and a dividend cut/elimination is implied by the math even though management has not announced one in this 10-K.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Buybacks already eliminated. Dividend is the next domino — the 10-K maintains 'subject to determination of our Board of Directors' boilerplate but offers no FCF reconciliation showing the dividend is sustainable. Mode-B inference: dividend cut probability is high given covenant amendments + rating negative outlook + $3.36B supplier-finance exposure. Investor-relations friendly framing masks the math.

rfm_tuples.R: 'Our compliance with these covenants will depend upon achieving our financial targets including improvements in operating income.' + 'We currently expect to be in compliance with these financial covenants for the next 12 months.' + cost-savings claim: 'We have identified and are pursuing cost reductions that we expect will generate at least $150 million in savings on an annualized basis, of which, we intend to invest approximately $50 million in employee compensation and training.'
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A — Verify magnitude of cost-reduction claim against the operating-income gap; Mode B — derive: $150M gross / $100M net cost-out is insufficient to bridge to even the loosest covenant step (Consolidated Coverage Ratio 2.00x by Q4'24) given the 83% YoY op-income decline
rfm_tuples.M_value: Op-income gap from 2022 to 2023: $670M - $114M = $556M. Promised cost-out: $150M gross / ~$100M net. Even full delivery closes only ~18-27% of the operating-income hole. To get to 2.00x Consolidated Coverage Ratio by Dec 2024, AAP needs both the cost-out AND a material gross-margin recovery AND interest-expense flat — none of which is bridged in the MD&A. Late-filing pattern (NT 10-K filed 2024-02-28, then 10-K filed 2024-03-12) and the prior-period NT 10-Q (filed 2023-11-17 for Q3'23) confirm the finance organization is operating in fire-drill mode.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: The 'expect to be in compliance for next 12 months' assertion is contingent on a cost-reduction program insufficient by 3-4x to close the operating-income gap to the new covenant floors. Two NT (notification of late filing) submissions in the 7 months preceding the 10-K are themselves an undisclosed signal of process distress. Compliance forecast is aspirational, not arithmetic.

Neutral-to-slightly-positive insider posture — does not align with worst-case distress narrative but is consistent with restricted-window mechanics.

Worldpac and Carquest Canada divestiture announcement (first appeared Q3'23 10-Q)
Negative Moody's outlook (vs no negative-outlook disclosure in FY2022 10-K)

Claim-evolution velocity is the highest-severity Mode-B signal — the FY2022 10-K reads as a stable specialty retailer, the FY2023 10-K reads as a turnaround/restructuring candidate. The pre-cutoff drawdown of -36.9% appears proportionate to the disclosed deterioration.

late_filings.interpretation: Two NT filings in 7 months preceding the 10-K — operating-control distress symptom even though both reports were ultimately filed within the 15/5-day grace periods.

summary: AAP's FY2023 10-K (filed 2024-03-12) contains a confluence of forensic red flags rare for a specialty-retail issuer: adverse ICFR opinion from Deloitte for a 13-month-persistent material weakness, $101M+ cumulative prior-period 'immaterial' error revisions, two covenant amendments within four months that progressively loosen the Consolidated Coverage Ratio with a back-end tightening schedule, CFO and CAO replacements during the same year, two NT-filing notifications, an 83% YoY operating-income collapse on flat revenue, a $3.36B supplier-finance program balance (80% of total AP, 6.7x cash) explicitly dependent on the company's split-rating that already carries a Moody's negative outlook, and a strategic-review divestiture of Worldpac and Carquest Canada that the FY2022 10-K did not mention. Going-concern language is absent and insider Form 4 activity is grant-dominated (not selling), which provides partial counterweight, but the dominant Mode-B inference is that a one-notch Moody's downgrade triggers a supplier-finance contraction whose magnitude dwarfs available liquidity. Verdict: SHORT-tier — multiple SEVERE_UNDERDELIVERY signals with reinforcing causal mechanism (margin collapse -> covenant amendment -> rating pressure -> supplier-finance dependence -> working-capital tail risk).
